A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same STERGM change-point detection framework. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v4 reports original SBM and STERGM simulations in Tables 1–6 and original analyses of MIT cellphone and stock-market data in Sections 5.2–5.3.

after.justification: v5 reports original simulations, real-data analyses, runtime measurements, and an appendix ablation study, including Tables 1–10 and 13.

M1.justification: The pseudolikelihood objective, weighted Group Fused Lasso, ADMM updates, BIC selection, and threshold formula are retained. Nodal-attribute support already appears in v4's homophily simulation; its application to additional real-data statistics changes experimental specifications, rather than introducing a method component.

E1.justification: v5 retains the SBM and STERGM simulations and both real datasets, while adding a temporally dependent Random Dot Product Graph Model scenario with evolving latent node positions. This substantially broadens the evaluated data-generating conditions beyond v4's two simulation families.

E2.justification: v5 adds CPDrdpg, CPDnbs, and CPDker alongside retained gSeg and kerSeg. These additions participate in the existing SBM and STERGM comparisons and real-data figures, not merely the new RDPGM experiment.

E3.justification: Simulation node counts change from {50,100,500} to {50,100,200}, and the lambda grid narrows from powers 10^-2 through 10^7 to 10^0 through 10^4. Both real-data experiments add degree-derived homophily statistics and change the threshold quantile from 0.9 to 0.975. v5 also changes the empty-detection reverse Hausdorff convention from negative to positive infinity and introduces RDPGM, timing, and ablation protocols.

E4.justification: v5 adds an ablation of adaptive penalty updates and position-dependent weights in Appendix E, Table 13. It also adds computational-cost comparisons in Section 5.1.1, Table 10, and raster-based examinations of the real-data detections in Figures 6 and 8. These address questions absent from v4's analyses.

E5.justification: The stated Monte Carlo count increases from 10 to 15 per configuration. v5 first reports standard deviations for change-point count and Hausdorff errors; coverage remains a point estimate. This is a limited expansion of replication and uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Existing simulation means are revised under changed protocols: for example, Table 1's SBM rho=0, n=100 coverage entry changes from 89.07% to 91.34%. v5 adds baseline, RDPGM, runtime, and ablation results and replaces 500-node entries with 200-node entries. Under revised real-data specifications, the MIT detection on 2004-11-02 disappears, and the stock-market plot retains only the three principal detections.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendix D introduce a conditional parameter-estimation error bound and consistency argument using bounded parameters, structured sparsity, restricted strong convexity, and a gradient dual-norm condition. The original optimizer derivations remain despite changed proposition numbering. The new proof contains an invalid norm inequality immediately before Equation (52).

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction promote nodal-attribute capability to an explicit contribution and remove BIC from their contribution statements, although BIC remains in Section 4.3. The central STERGM/GFL/ADMM contribution and claims about detecting vacations and three financial events remain.

C2.justification: v5 substantially expands the pseudolikelihood rationale, arguing that conditioning reduces dependence and localization can tolerate coefficient-estimation bias. It adds interpretations of the runtime tradeoff, degree-derived covariates, raster patterns, and component ablation. Existing binary-network and changing-node limitations remain, while multilayer and contrastive-learning extensions are newly discussed.

D1.justification: A new Code and Data Availability section supplies a CPDstergm_demo reproduction-code link and explicitly locates the MIT data in CPDstergm; v4 supplies the main package link. v5 also documents degree-median attribute construction and the added comparators' packages and hyperparameters.

R1.justification: The central related-work positioning remains, with additions supporting pseudolikelihood exposition, RDPGM experiments, and estimation theory, including Negahban et al. (2012), Hütter and Rigollet (2016), and Lin et al. (2017). Multilayer and contrastive-learning references are added. The Song–Chen and Kei et al. title/publication updates are matched as retained works.

P1.justification: The six-section narrative and much of the existing prose are retained. Changes include expanded pseudolikelihood explanations, revised subsection titles, model selection moved before thresholding, references moved before appendices, and updated author information. These are localized editorial and structural revisions alongside the scientific additions.

P2.justification: v5 adds an RDPGM illustration, two raster plots, runtime and ablation tables, and expanded benchmark displays with mean–standard-deviation formatting. Real-data comparison plots are redrawn with additional comparators. v4's network-statistic Tables 9–11 are consolidated into v5 Table 14, and typography and title-page layout change throughout.

improvement.justification: The broader comparisons, RDPGM evaluation, ablation, runtime evidence, and reproduction-code information improve empirical support and transparency. These gains are tempered by losing the 500-node evaluations and introducing a proof gap: the inequality before Appendix D's Equation (52) fails for adjacent errors -1 and 1, whose squared difference is 4 but squared norm is 2. The new theoretical guarantee is therefore not established as written, limiting the overall improvement.
